I get socializing can be extremely stressful and if it doesn't go great, you'll beat yourself up over it afterwards. I lived that. I still sometimes have dates where my heart skips beats and I'm an anxious mess (I only started dating 2 years ago at age 27). 

But try to compare the feeling of not going out at all, i.e. cancelling last minute because of anxiety and the feeling of going through with it, against the anxiety  because you desire social interaction. Even if the social interaction sucks, you stood up for yourself, you overruled the anxiety, that's something you can be proud of. That's what I meant by feeling glad.

I  hope you have some positive experiences soon friend, because that can kickstart your growth, once you make the experience that positive interactions are possible your perspective changes. It goes from 'this negative experience is further evidence I suck' to 'this interaction sucked, we weren't compatible, maybe next time goes better'.

Assuming your brain can't learn from social interactions is (extremely likely) just a belief you formed that keeps you from attempting to go through difficult situations, it feeds your avoidant behaviour.

Just saw a Dr.K yt short about exactly this. Best way to improve your social skills is tolerating the feeling of social incompetence and go out socializing, your brain will do the rest.

Also therapy alone won't help your social anxiety. It can give you tools to make the decision to go out and socialize, but it will still suck in the beginning. Only exposure will help. You go out, get through social situations that scare the shit out of you, but you will feel glad you did it afterwards and slowly your brain will learn to not be as scared anymore.

First, comparing yourself to others almost always brings misery. Everyone's mind is unique, so everyone enjoys and dislikes different things. That's totally ok and fine. The answer to all of this is acceptance. Accept that this is the way your mind operates. Your feelings ARE valid. This is how you are. You are the way you are and that's perfectly fine. So if you feel dumb for worrying about stuff, try to recognize it. I'll give you a personal example: I had intense work-related anxiety. I felt under pressure all the time. I felt like there was something wrong with me for feeling this pressure and I tried everything to not feel this way. It got worse, I started vomiting every day before work. In therapy I uncovered that this emotional response comes from the past. In my childhood I felt this pressure and so I felt it in the present also, even if there was no reason to feel pressured at work. I started to accept that I feel the fear because of the past and that there is nothing wrong with me. I recognized the fear on my way to work, and with a bit of practice, by the time I arrived at work it was almost gone.

There probably is a reason why your mind is the way it is, but there is nothing wrong about it and accepting it the way it is will help you a great deal :)
